sample_unit: suspicious pigmented lesions (diagnostic trial; 124 patients); management trial 5696 lesions from 66 patients

links.outcome: Real-world clinical accuracy of AI versus experimental (online reader study) performance
links.effect: The ISIC AI algorithm, superior in experimental studies, was significantly inferior to specialists in the clinic (-11·6% [-20·3 to -3·0]) for diagnosis.
links.quote: An AI algorithm that was superior in experimental studies was significantly inferior to specialists in a real-world scenario, suggesting that caution is needed when extrapolating results of experimental studies to clinical practice.

links.outcome: Diagnostic and management accuracy of AI versus specialist and novice clinicians on same lesions
links.effect: 7-class AI equivalent to specialists (1·2% [-6·9 to 9·2]) and superior to novices (21·5%); ISIC AI inferior to specialists (-11·6%); management AI inferior to specialists (-0·5% scenario A).
links.quote: The diagnoses of the 7-class AI algorithm were equivalent to the specialists' diagnoses (absolute accuracy difference 1·2% [95% CI -6·9 to 9·2]) and significantly superior to the novices' ones (21·5% [13·1 to 30·0]).

screen.reason: Multicentre prospective diagnostic clinical trial comparing the diagnostic and management accuracy of mobile phone-based AI against novice and expert clinicians on real patients in secondary care, but without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
